speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We have made substantial progress in child protection and children's rights, as illustrated in our 2019 report to the Committee on the Rights of the Child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We continue to receive international attention and praise for our success as a nation and public safety and security is at the heart of everything we do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore is forward looking, and we do this well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are experts at monitoring our landscape, anticipating changes, and planning for the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The report describes Singapore's road map for the next decade and beyond, and highlights the need to reimagine the Singapore Dream, refresh our social compact, and redefine success as seen from the lens of our younger generation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We are advancing towards creating a better future for Singapore and we are doing this in consultation with the people of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am excited with this progress as this is home not just for me, but also for my children and their children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As we evolve, we want to ensure the progression of everyone, and especially our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As a nation, we need to continue to promote and protect the safety and wellbeing of children, and to work together to nurture and support all children to reach their potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: On that note, let me take you on an adventure, through the lens of Lewis Carroll's "Alice in Wonderland" that resonates with my Adjournment Motion, "Child Safety and Well-being: A Collective Responsibility".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And I believe there is no limitation when it comes to dreams.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Many of these children succeeded despite great hardship and their success reminds me of the need to set goals and work diligently towards a dreamt future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As social workers, we operate with a clear vision in mind, and the safety and wellbeing of our clients is our paramount consideration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We also believe in establishing clear goals, for our clients, and it is timely for me to share my favourite quote from Alice in Wonderland: "If you don't know where you are going, any road can take you there." Since 1999, when I was working as a social worker in a children's home and subsequently as a probation officer, I have observed many changes that illustrate Singapore's strong commitment to protecting children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We have come a long way, and I would like to commend the efforts taken by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), in driving these changes, and for constantly reviewing our social compact.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Most importantly, I would like to acknowledge the good work done by those who work with children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: At this juncture, I would like to share another quote from Alice in Wonderland, where the Queen says to Alice: "Now, here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: If you want to get somewhere else, you must run at least twice as fast as that!" While Singapore has undoubtedly done well, today's Adjournment Motion is about moving forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And, as the Queen encourages Alice, we need to run at least twice as fast.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I would, however, like to stress that this is not merely about running quickly and arriving breathless.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This Motion is about defining a goal, setting a steady pace, and arriving at our destination composed and confident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This Motion is also about considering the principles that augment Singapore's efforts in safeguarding children, adopting a collective responsibility and articulating a united direction and methodology to ensure a better future for our children and our nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They may fall off a swing in a playground, they may be bullied at school, or they may get abused or harmed by someone close to them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is unrealistic to expect a world entirely free from such complexities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Risk is multifaceted, and there is no single solution that can entirely reduce the presence of risk, or harm from happening.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, each of us has a role to play – and it begins with family.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   As we know, and we continue to strengthen this part of our social compact – family is our first line of defence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The family plays a significant role in nurturing and protecting a child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The traditional concept of family, however, is changing – from nuclear families, into reconstituted families or single-parent families or even the no-parent families – and this is a challenge, especially when it comes to differences in parenting and disciplinary style.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Most of us who are parents would agree that parenting is an adventure that comes with many surprises.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And yet, there is no one standard rule book for this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Parents tend to replicate the practices of their own parents, which can perpetuate both positive and negative parenting methods, leading to differences in viewpoints within marriages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We know from studies that inadequate preparation for parental roles contributes to problems like child abuse, neglect and strained parent-child relationships.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore, most parents need to work to support the family and many of us rely on extended families, helpers and childcare facilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And yet, the involvement from both parents is crucial in ensuring safety and wellbeing of our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: There is also a greater need for fathers to play a role in child upbringing and this also requires support given to working mothers to balance their role within the home as a wife, mother and excel in their career aspiration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I am proud that we have various initiatives to strengthen parenting, and create a Singapore made for families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: On that note, as we develop our measures, we should consider ways to incorporate our gotong-royong spirit, and preserve our traditional family values of love, care and concern, filial responsibility and mutual respect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I would now like to suggest three initiatives to assist Singapore to take the next step in promoting and protecting the safety and wellbeing of our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: National frameworks are not just idealistic policy statements, they set clear targets, measurable outcomes and realistic timelines.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: A national framework will ensure that the best interests of children are at the centre of decision-making and will reaffirm Singapore's commitment to making our nation the best place in the world for children to live and thrive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Importantly, national frameworks are not designed to address one-off incidents or issues but reflect a systematic, long-term approach to improving the safety and well-being of our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore, most children do okay, most of the time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: A national framework will help all children do okay, all the time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They ensure that decision-makers consider the specific needs and vulnerabilities of children when making decisions, they promote child-centered decision-making, they help governments create laws, policies and programmes that are responsive to the specific needs of children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Child impact assessments have been endorsed by the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child and have been successfully implemented in several countries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In some countries, these take the form of a Children's Commissioner, a Children's Guardian or a Children's Ombudsman, or they may have a more targeted role such as a E-Safety Commissioner or a National Office for Child Safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The first Children's Commissioner was established in Norway in 1981.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Regardless of their title, what these offices have in common is that they are stand-alone agencies with a focus on promoting and protecting the safety and well-being of children, providing impartial advice to the government and advocating for the rights of children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Forward Singapore was an opportunity for Singaporeans to come together and examine the nation's values and aspirations, build consensus and to refresh the social compact.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As observed by former President Madam Halimah Yaacob when commenting on the initiative at the opening of the Second Session of the 14th Parliament on 10 April 2023, I quote, "We want every person to be treated equally with dignity and respect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We want a Singapore where everyone belongs, and every citizen has the chance to achieve his or her fullest potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We want a society that values and supports families; where we care for and help one another, and pitch in to make a difference to our community." As Singapore moves forward, we must speak and listen to our children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to bring together different groups of children, tap on their experiences and seek their views and opinions on how we can do things differently and do things better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, it is important that we engage with all children, not simply those who are already vocal or active within their community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to talk with children like those I met when I was a social worker and who told me repeatedly that they wanted to have a greater say in their future and the future of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Referring to the wisdom of the Cheshire Cat from Alice in Wonderland, "Let your need guide your behavior." Sir, the safety and wellbeing of children is not merely a duty, it is a reflection of our commitment to a better tomorrow, where every child is treated with respect and dignity and where their potential knows no bounds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our children are not merely extensions of ourselves but unique individuals with their own dreams and destinies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We, as a society, are entrusted with the responsibility of protecting and nurturing them, not to mould them into our image, but to help them flourish as the remarkable individuals they are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We must invest in their safety and well-being, not only because they deserve such care but because they hold the future of our nation in their hands.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They are the architects of tomorrow, the visionaries who will shape our society and the stewards of our collective destiny.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As we focus on their safety, health and growth, we must ensure that they have the strength and resilience to face the challenges of an ever-changing world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Let us remember that by protecting and nurturing our children, we are not just securing their future but also the future of our country, built upon the promise of their unique potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Indeed, we are united in our goal to advance our children's safety and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, it is this approach that enabled Singapore to make strides in online safety, education, security and child protection.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The National Council of Social Service surveys the quality of life of children and youths, using a common global standard.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In its study published in 2022, our children and youths report a high quality of life, comparable to their peers in developed countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2021, the UK charity Save the Children ranked Singapore as the top country where childhood is most protected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government has been and will continue to commit to ensure the safety and well-being of our children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We offer good, affordable and accessible healthcare to keep our children healthy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also provide accessible, affordable and quality education that starts from preschool.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have developed national mental health and well-being strategies to address risks and promote mental health and well-being for youths with such concerns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also have robust protocols and processes for our child protection ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From this strong foundation, we must indeed move forward for Singapore's children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In doing so, we must not forget that strong families are the bedrock of our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Strong and resilient families nurture children to become strong individuals and active and compassionate members of our society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As families navigate various milestones in their life journey, we want to ensure parents are equipped with skills to build safe havens for their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families can receive support from the Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centres.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These provide marriage support programmes for young couples and family counselling to help families navigate marital and parent-child relationship issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We give additional support to lower income parents through KidSTART.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: KidSTART equips parents with the knowledge and skills to nurture their children's development and helps them build stronger bonds with their children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: KidSTART, which now comes under the larger umbrella of ComLink+, helps to better ensure that the needs of the children from lower-income households are met, in partnership with preschools and other community partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through ComLink+, we assign the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) family coaches to journey with these families and partner them in navigating life's challenges and seize opportunities to build a better future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our ultimate goal is to enable ComLink+ families to achieve stability, self-reliance and, eventually, social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To ensure the safety and well-being of vulnerable children, MSF has strengthened information-sharing and coordination protocols with various touchpoints in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Frontline professionals in preschools, schools, healthcare institutions and social service agencies are trained to identify and report child abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Break the Silence campaign educates and encourages the public to report suspected violence or neglect.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The amendments strengthen powers for the Government to rehabilitate perpetrators, which is crucial to helping families reconcile once protection and safety for victim-survivors, including children, have been achieved.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When parents continue to fail or are unable to keep their child safe, MSF's Child Protective Service (CPS) will intervene to remove the child as a last resort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: CPS, together with relevant professionals and community partners, works to stabilise and rebuild family relationships so that the children can be safely reunited, wherever possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We note the Member's suggestion to set up a dedicated Office for Child Safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is much lower compared to other countries, including those that have opted for a standalone Child Safety agency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, we already have a specialised agency for child protection in the form of the Child Protective Service (CPS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the same time, we recognise that child safety takes place in the context of a family situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: That is why the CPS is part of a larger Rehabilitation and Protection Group in MSF, which also includes the Adult Protective Service as well as the Probation and Community Rehabilitation Service, to help youths who are in the justice system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF will continue to work closely with agencies and community partners to detect, identify and provide care and support for child survivors of different forms of abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our policies are also well coordinated in Singapore through an Inter-Ministry Committee that oversees the implementation of national policies relating to children and their progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF, as the lead agency, works with other agencies to ensure that Singapore's policies and practices consider the child's best interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have explained this to the United Nations Committee on the Convention on the Rights of the Child in our reports to and constructive dialogues with the Committee, with the assurance that safeguarding the best interests of our children is a shared objective that we will continue to uphold vigorously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These are enshrined in our legislation such as the Children and Young Persons Act and the Adoption of Children Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Outside of legislation, the various Ministries set targets and approaches on children-related policies and practices in their respective domains of expertise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, the inter-agency taskforce for Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy and Action Plan reviews and develops approaches to achieve better health outcomes for children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For children with disabilities, the Enabling Masterplan 2030 outlines the Government's priorities to scale up learning support and capacity for preschoolers and students in mainstream schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over the years, we have found this approach to be effective and sufficient.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a parent of a young three-year-old myself, I appreciate and echo the Member's call for the nation to continue to listen to the voices of our young ones on how Singapore can move forward and do things better.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is an important part of building a stronger society, and Singapore will continue to engage our children and youth to hear their voices and consider their best interests as we move forward.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: All of us have, indeed, a role to play to create a safer and better environment for our children, and support them to fulfil their hopes and dreams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And as a society, we will continue to press on to create a better future for our children and for our nation.
